props.title: Spanish guitar for private events, played by Dirty Flamenco.
props.lede: You know how it feels when a flamenco guitarist really gets going, and you can't take your eyes off those hands? Dirty Flamenco is a flamenco trio led by guitarist Gary Meyers, with bass and cajón (a box drum). The trio can play quietly through cocktails and dinner, and we can plan a featured performance for the moment you'd like everyone to stop and watch.

headingText.html: Dirty Flamenco is a great pick for dinner parties, milestone birthdays, member events and corporate dinners. Prefer one musician? Check out our Spanish guitarist, who's a lovely fit for a ceremony or a cocktail hour.

props.headingNote: We can plan the music around your event, including the songs, whether you'd like a dancer and what the trio wears. Here’s how booking through Signet works.

props.title: How does a flamenco trio fit into an event?

props.html: The trio can play through your whole event, and the featured performance is when they really let loose. Just let us know where you'd like it in the flow of the evening, and our run of show guide can help you plan it.
The trio can also play slower or livelier to suit your event.

props.title: Watch Dirty Flamenco play live
props.lede: Here's the trio playing live, along with a few clips of Gary Meyers on guitar. You'll hear a Malagueña, a rumba, a farruca, tangos, a piece by the flamenco guitarist Sabicas, Can’t Help Falling in Love and three guitars on Entre dos Aguas.

rows.text: Flamenco is a great way to give a member or association event some color and a sense of occasion.
A short flamenco performance can give a corporate dinner a high point, and we'll plan it around your program.
A flamenco trio can turn a dinner at home into a real occasion, indoors or out in the backyard. It's one of the best fits for the trio, too.

The trio can play a fiftieth or sixtieth birthday, an anniversary or a retirement party, in Denver or up in the mountains. The music gives the party a centerpiece, so the guest of honor can just enjoy it.

rows.term: The wedding ceremony and cocktail hour
rows.text: The trio can play your prelude, your processional and your recessional, and then keep the flamenco going through the cocktail hour.

items.q: Does Dirty Flamenco play traditional flamenco or Spanish guitar?
items.a: It's traditional flamenco first, and the trio plays covers too. Spanish guitar can also mean familiar songs with a Spanish flavor, and that's closer to what our solo Spanish guitarist plays. You can book Dirty Flamenco through Signet Artists in Denver.

During dinner, the trio can keep things soft enough for your guests to carry on talking. The featured performance will be louder, since that's the part you'll want everyone to watch. The trio can adjust to the venue and your crowd. If your venue has a sound limit, just let us know and they'll play within it.

items.q: Is Spanish guitar right for a wedding ceremony?
items.a: Yes. It's a beautiful sound for a wedding ceremony, and the trio can move between Spanish pieces and the songs you ask for.
Yes. The dancer becomes the star of the featured performance. Just let us know when you send us the date.
